limitations: not a rustc-level resolution: trait-object dispatch, generics, closures and macro-expanded call edges are not resolved; the graph over-approximates call edges by name and under-approximates dynamic dispatch

re-exports (`pub use private_mod::x`) are not followed; a pub fn in a private module re-exported is counted as external only if its own module chain is pub, so the external count is a lower bound for that shape
fn-level attributes on the same line as the signature are captured; attributes are matched by balanced brackets on stripped text

mechanism_files_are_clean_of_the_raw_poi.basis: the scanner's own per-mechanism records filtered on safe, definition, direct_unsafe, raw_pointer_param and vis == pub

safe_pub_surface_at_candidate.review_cohort_covers_the_safe_surface_on: the reviews read unsafe declarations and their callers; the safe pub fns that reach unsafe in the mechanism files are not themselves the subject of a per-function review, so criterion 3 for the safe surface rests on the reviews' caller analysis, not on a dedicated safe-interface audit.

callbacks_reentrancy.why: the mechanisms are dominated by provider dispatch tables, stack free/dup thunks, X509V3 method callbacks, BIO method tables, the CONF_METHOD cell, ENGINE free hooks and ex_data
callbacks_reentrancy.residual: 116 reachable unresolved sites are contract-bounded by public ABI (0 target-bounded, 0 unclassified) and are discharged only under section 7 criterion 2; no TSan/Loom/runtime reentrancy test at S; SSL_SESSION retains external serialisation for a concurrent free and a release race.

aliasing_ownership.why: the owner family and the provider copyctx self-copy arm are the shared ownership mechanism; the recent conversions touched release contracts in cms_lib.rs, cms_asn1.rs, rand_lib.rs and the SAN builders
aliasing_ownership.residual: no Miri run at S; the operation-span hash excludes caller closures; the reconversion review's D1 (11/12 qualifier-control tests self-satisfying), D2 (SSL_COMP_get_name has no effective qualifier control) and D5 (OPENSSL_init_ssl # Safety under-specifies the settings obligations) are open; b80-rebind R2 (the two CMS free # Safety texts say 'exactly-once release' where the call releases a reference) is OPEN.

panic_safety.why: the C ABI edge uses guard_ffi with AssertUnwindSafe; catching a panic does not repair partially mutated state (AGENTS.md section 4)
panic_safety.residual: no failure-atomicity, rollback or poison-state evidence for any stateful context in the closure at S

secret_memory.why: RAND_CMS_STORE_KEYFMT covers CMS/PEM key material and SSL_SESSION covers session secrets; release and cleansing are separate obligations
secret_memory.residual: clear-free arms are preserved and reviewed in the CMS release paths, but secret cleansing is not audited as a category, and no timing/leakage instrument ran at S

verdict.decision_rule: SAFETY_DISCHARGED only if every obligation in the mechanism has an explicit validity contract, every required precondition is established by its callers at the candidate, and no safe interface can cause UB. OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED only if a safe ownership model exists and the residual boundary is identified without an unestablished caller precondition. Otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED.
verdict.statement: At b85c the receipt basis is re-established under the repaired verifier: both consumer closures are ACCEPTED with all 290 reachable production obligations DISCHARGED, 0 BLOCKED and 0 UNKNOWN, and element 7 PASS (116 external ABI contracts + 36 closed target sets). That is a predicate the b85 receipts did not have to meet. The substantive argument is otherwise unchanged from b85 and still establishes only two mechanisms under explicitly scoped claims: SSL_SESSION (unchanged) and RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY (clean TSan at b80 on byte-identical concurrency files, schedule-bounded). The four internal safe-surface holes and the SHA-256 Final staging-buffer aliasing UB are closed at 5edca576b, with Miri reporting 0 UB on the six digest tests under both borrow models; the b84 safe-surface audit closes condition 3 for the X509 (69/69 nullary) and RAND (17/17 nullary or c_int-only) external surfaces, and F-1 is registered. Neither X509 nor RAND nor EVP is discharged: X509 retains the v3_cpols per-row gap, the un-re-established caller closure and 120/122 instrument gaps; RAND retains the OPEN R2 release contract and missing instrument coverage; EVP retains R-1/R-2, the excluded dispatch surfaces and 171 unaudited internal safe fns. C_ABI_CONTRACT and BIO remain NOT_ESTABLISHED. Nothing here graduates a consumer family: safe_compatible stays false.

receipt_basis.acceptance_now_entails: no refusal fired and every row DISCHARGED

residuals.statement: 33 obligations live in files changed between the reviews' tree (5b08c0294) and S; 26 are re-established at S by content identity or by a b80/b81/b82/b83/b84/b85 rebind, and 7 are not: src/digest/sha2.rs::sha512_224_init and src/provider/conf.rs::provider_free_thunk (the b85 digest/conf repair), src/x509/v3_cpols.rs::i2r_certpol and ::r2i_certpol (no per-row verdict), and src/x509/v3_ncons.rs::i2r_NAME_CONSTRAINTS and ::v2i_NAME_CONSTRAINTS (byte-identical but not re-read), and src/pkcs7/pk7_asn1.rs::ri_cb (byte-identical but not re-read). They are counted as not re-established, not absorbed; the b85 repair's own rows are the new ones and are adjudicated by the Miri digest run and the unsafe-fn controls, not by a site re-read.

the three private X509 helpers fed1f077b elevated -- i2v_ainfo_err, v2i_ainfo_err (src/x509/v3_info.rs) and nc_email_eai (src/x509/v3_ncons.rs) -- are now `unsafe fn` with written ownership contracts, and their call sites state the witness. This removes a safe-Rust entry point that could free a caller-supplied stack (i2v/v2i) or read a caller-supplied ASN1_TYPE arm (nc_email_eai); it does not discharge X509_VERIFY_POLICY, whose review still declines mechanism-wide discharge. The three source-text qualifier controls are the only instrument that can detect a qualifier regression (a qualifier-removed mutant compiles with 8 `unnecessary unsafe block` warnings and fails exactly the three controls; that mutant ran at b82 and is NOT_RUN at b85 (unchanged from b84), while its baseline arm re-ran at b84 and passed); a semantically equivalent re-introduction of the same obligation behind a different safe signature would not be detected by that instrument and remains a review obligation.

b84 changed src/runtime/bio/bf_readbuff.rs only by replacing the two callbacks' `#[allow(clippy::missing_safety_doc)]` attributes with written `# Safety` contracts; b85 leaves the file unchanged. The mechanism remains UNSAFE_OPEN and only 2 of its production operations are in the closure, so BIO stays NOT_ESTABLISHED mechanism-wide.

X509_VERIFY_POLICY condition 3 is MET at b85 by the external-surface audit (69/69 nullary). The mechanism remains NOT_ESTABLISHED on condition 1's v3_cpols per-row gap, condition 2's un-re-established caller closure and 24 orphans, and condition 4 (120 of 122 obligations have no Miri/ASan test).

RAND_CMS_STORE_KEYFMT condition 3 is MET at b85 (17/17 external safe pub fns nullary or c_int-only). It remains NOT_ESTABLISHED on R2 (the CMS free contracts still say 'exactly-once release' where the stack's reference is released) and on condition 4 (rand_lib/cmp/pkcs7 rows have no instrument coverage).

EVP_PKEY_PROVIDER: the four internal holes are closed at 5edca576b (two unsafe fns, two &CStr helpers) and F-1 is registered, but R-1/R-2, the review's excluded OSSL_OP_* surfaces and 171 unaudited internal safe fns keep it NOT_ESTABLISHED.
C_ABI_CONTRACT and BIO: UNSAFE_OPEN mechanism-wide; the closure's 5 and 2 sites are site arguments, not mechanism discharge; F-EVID-1/F-EVID-2 remain.

the closure tool's --self-test exits 0 with 0 failures under the repaired instrument at b85c (court/freeze-b85/review15/selftest.log, instrument 3e86a74d), and the 14 fixture controls in review15/controls.json include the replayed 37-BLOCKED receipt that the b85 predicate accepted. This is a tool control result, not a safety result; the b85 self-test ran under b42f19bd.

the four crate-internal safe fns the b84 audit named are closed at 5edca576b: sha256_block and sha512_block are unsafe fns with extent/disjointness contracts (their callers are unsafe blocks) and matches_any/same take &CStr. This removes the four caller-memory preconditions from the safe surface; it does not audit the remaining 171 internal safe fns that reach unsafe in the EVP files, which stay a named residual.

the X509 (69) and RAND (17) external safe pub fns are audited nullary/c_int-only in evidence/b84-safe-pub-audit.json, so no external safe caller can pass memory the mechanism assumes valid. This closes criterion 3 for those surfaces only; it is not a mechanism-wide discharge and does not establish the caller closures, the per-row receipts or the missing instrument coverage.

the b85 receipts were ACCEPTED under a predicate that did not refuse BLOCKED rows, so their ACCEPTED did not entail a fully-DISCHARGED closure. The b85c re-run under 3e86a74d (committed at b14923bda) reports all 290 reachable production obligations DISCHARGED, 0 BLOCKED, 0 UNKNOWN, no refusal and element 7 PASS for both families; each receipt differs from its b85 predecessor only as classified in court/freeze-b85/review16/receipt-delta-{ssh,sshd}.json. The closure still derives most rows by carry-forward: 280 of 290 rows carry the b84b-era discharge forward through b85 to b85c, so this rebind re-attests those discharges at a new instrument and does not re-derive them from source. The 111 committed receipts that the repaired predicate now refuses remain refused and are not covered by this rebind.

the b85 review-rebind and artefact-ledger receipts record instrument b42f19bd and were NOT re-run under 3e86a74d in this pass. The instrument delta is confined to refusal synthesis and the verdict predicate, which no rebind row consumes (the rebind reads predicate_element_7 and span resolution), but the re-execution is recorded as NOT_RUN rather than asserted. The L4 and L7 receipts are likewise unchanged and were not re-measured here.
